selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state captured before restart (boot identity, cmdline, audit state)
selected_evidence.summary: Captured initial /proc/cmdline (no audit=1), boot_id 33b0e84c-4dd1-406a-8f89-2e8ceca97bd6, uptime -s, and auditctl -s showing kernel audit enabled=0 prior to change taking effect

selected_evidence.requirement: audit=1 added to GRUB config and applied to all kernel entries for persistence
selected_evidence.summary: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub updated with audit=1; grubby applied audit=1 to both the default and rescue kernel entries; grub.cfg on-disk linux16 lines confirmed to include audit=1 for both entries

selected_evidence.requirement: Single node restarted one at a time with acknowledgement returned before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: `sudo systemctl reboot` issued on node1; command returned reboot-issued acknowledgement and then the SSH connection closed, confirming the restart was triggered

selected_evidence.requirement: Node polled until reachable again, with proof of changed boot identity (not just elapsed time)
selected_evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node still rebooting); second poll succeeded and returned a new boot_id (dddcd817-01b0-4754-83d8-61a7339135f6) differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual kernel restart occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart proof that audit=1 is active and persisted across reboot
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, /proc/cmdline includes audit=1, auditctl -s reports kernel audit enabled=1 (changed from 0 pre-restart), and dmesg shows the audit subsystem initializing at boot, confirming the kernel booted with audit=1 and the setting survives reboot
